content:
The first public beta of iOS 27 is now available for iPhone users to download, allowing everyone to experience Apple's most important system update of the year ahead of time.

Siri AI is the most eye-catching new feature in this update. This update also brings a redesigned "Screen Time" experience, Liquid Glass interface optimisations, performance improvements, and dozens of changes that improve everyday usability.

Below we will introduce how to install the beta, the latest features, and which features are worth trying first.

Table of Contents

  • How to join the iOS 27 public beta
  • Siri AI is the most important feature of iOS 27
  • Apple Intelligence brings AI features to more iPhone apps
  • iOS 27 makes Liquid Glass more personalisable and flexible
  • iOS 27 runs more smoothly overall, and older iPhones benefit too
  • A major revamp for Screen Time and child safety features
  • More features worth trying in the iOS 27 public beta
  • 9to5Mac Perspective
  • Get the most out of your Apple products

The Apple Beta Software Program is free and open, with no developer account required.

Before installing, please back up your iPhone to iCloud or a computer. Beta software may contain bugs, shorten battery life, and cause compatibility issues with some third-party apps.

The steps to enrol and install the beta are as follows:

  • Go to the Apple Beta Software Program website and choose "Sign Up" to register or "Sign In" to log in.
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account on your iPhone, then accept the programme terms and register your account.
  • Open "Settings" on your iPhone.
  • Go to "General" > "Software Update" > "Beta Updates".
  • Select "iOS 27 Public Beta".
  • Return to the "Software Update" screen, and when the beta appears, tap "Update Now".

Apple recommends installing the beta on a device that is not your primary one. If you plan to install it on your daily main iPhone, be sure to make a recent backup first.

iOS 27 supports all iPhone models that can run iOS 26, including the iPhone 11 and later models, as well as the 2nd generation or newer iPhone SE.

However, Apple Intelligence requires an iPhone 15 Pro or later. Apple's most powerful new on-device models have even stricter hardware requirements, but Siri AI can run on any iPhone that meets the Apple Intelligence compatibility requirements.

After installing the iOS 27 public beta, we recommend starting your experience with Siri AI.

Apple has rebuilt Siri from the ground up based on the next-generation Apple Intelligence system. The assistant can now hold ongoing conversations and search your personal information; it can also understand what's on your screen, perform actions within apps, and answer a broader range of questions.

Siri's responses will emerge from the Dynamic Island, and pulling down expands the response into a full conversation. In addition, a standalone Siri app will centrally store all conversation history and sync it privately via iCloud.

After installing the public beta, you can try asking Siri to find a specific piece of information buried in "Mail", "Messages", "Notes", "Reminders" or "Calendar", and then ask follow-up questions without repeating the original request. In iOS 27 beta 3, Siri has also begun accessing data provided by some third-party apps.

The "Camera" app adds a new Siri mode for Visual Intelligence. For example, you can snap a membership barcode and convert it into a Wallet pass; Siri can also import event details from a flyer.

In addition, Apple has added options to control Siri's speech rate and tone, adjustable under "Settings" > "Siri & Search" > "Siri Voice". These settings also affect voice output in "Maps" and Safari.

Siri AI initially only supports a few English-language regions, will not launch immediately in the EU, and requires an iPhone compatible with Apple Intelligence. As for some advanced on-device features, they require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, or iPhone Air.

The iOS 27 public beta extends some of the best AI features beyond Siri into other areas.

Safari can automatically organise tabs by topic, categorise bookmarks and Reading List items, and show recently closed topics on the start page. In addition, the "Notify Me" feature can monitor web pages for changes, such as a product being back in stock; Safari can even generate custom extensions based on natural language descriptions.

"Photos" gains three powerful editing tools: "Clean Up" can handle larger and more complex distractions; "Extend" generates content beyond the original frame; and "Spatial Re framing" lets you adjust the perspective composition of a shot after taking it.

You can try "Extend" to fix photos with a tilted horizon, and then try "Spatial Re-framing" to adjust poorly composed portraits.

The "Passwords" app can automatically replace eligible passwords that are too weak or have been compromised, handle verification codes, and show progress via "Live Activities". "Shortcuts" can now create automation routines based on natural language commands, and can keep describing changes to refine the results.

Other new additions to Apple Intelligence include:

  • "Call Context" in the "Phone" app, which displays information such as reservation numbers when you call a business.
  • More photorealistic image generation added to "Image Playground", along with natural language editing features.
  • "Calendar" supports creating and editing events using natural language.

iOS 27 does not replace last year's Liquid Glass design language, but instead focuses on clarity and flexibility.

Controls are now more effective at de-emphasising complex background content; darker edges and brighter highlights also bring a more pronounced sense of depth, making buttons and text easier to read. App icons gain more depth and dimension.

The first feature worth trying is a new custom slider for Liquid Glass, found under "Settings" > "Appearance". The slider ranges from fully transparent to fully tinted, and applies to iOS system and third-party apps.

The speed improvements Apple has promised with iOS 27 aren't limited to the latest hardware. The company says app launches can be up to 30% faster; nearby AirDrop transfers can complete up to 80% faster; and newly shot photos can appear in "Photos" up to 70% faster.

Apple has optimised the CPU scheduler all the way back to the iPhone 11. At the same time, unlocking, navigating the home screen, scrolling in Control Centre, and switching between Lock Screens are all smoother; opening the camera in Low Power Mode is also faster.

iOS 27 is also smarter about switching between Wi-Fi and cellular data, so when you leave home your iPhone is less likely to stay on a weak network than before. Search in Spotlight, "Photos", and "Mail" has also been rebuilt, and "Mail" can now display up to five ranked "Top Hits" in search results.

iOS 27 brings a major revamp to Screen Time and parental controls features. A new dashboard gives parents clearer visibility into their children's usage and offers one-tap shortcuts to change settings.

"App Time Limits" can set time limits for categories such as "Games", "Entertainment", and "Social Media"; "Schedules" can control which apps can be used at different times. Parents can set up separate rules for school days, after school, and weekends.

"Ask Before Browsing" extends the familiar "Ask Before Buying" flow to websites. Children can also request approval before contacting new people. The "Communication Safety" feature already detects and blurs nudity; iOS 27 further adds the ability to intervene when bloody or violent content is detected.

One important note: the new experience requires that all devices participating in "Family Sharing" must be running an OS 27 generation system.

The following small refinements add up to a significant overall effect:

  • "Messages" will continue sending large media files in the background without blocking newer conversations; it will also consolidate "Tapback" notifications within group chats.
  • "Photos" adds full-resolution shared albums, shared album joining for Windows and Android users, keywords, star ratings, and customisable slideshows.
  • You can save any frame from a video as a photo with one tap.
  • Alarm volume can be adjusted independently of system volume.
  • Extra-large widgets can fill an entire home screen page.
  • AirPods gain customisable equaliser settings for bass, mid, and treble.
  • iPhone can connect directly to compatible GymKit fitness equipment.
  • FaceTime supports video calls using the front and rear cameras simultaneously on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 models.
  • The "Home" app adds more stable HomeKit Secure Video functionality and supports native 4K cameras via compatible hardware and iCloud+.

The iOS 27 public beta will continue to be updated throughout the summer, and Apple is expected to release the final version in the autumn. If you encounter issues, you can use the built-in "Feedback Assistant" app to report them directly to Apple.

9to5Mac Perspective

iOS 27 is a very impressive update. We're right in the middle of summer, and most iOS beta experiences are still somewhat rough around the edges. iOS 27 isn't perfect, but it already delivers a noticeably crisp upgrade over iOS 26.

I'm really fond of the new Liquid Glass slider. I tried cranking it all the way to the most transparent (far left), expecting that I'd prefer something more dramatic; instead, the most opaque setting (far right) felt best — both in look and feel — modern without feeling dated.

I started out on a Mac running OS X Leopard, moved up to Snow Leopard fairly quickly, and then spent longer stretches on OS X Lion and Mountain Lion. I never actually lived through Mac's Aqua interface, but Liquid Glass's new look (set to far right) gives off a vibe of a modern-day Aqua on iOS.

Siri AI is also a clear winner. It's responsive, capable, and looks and sounds great — and on the whole brings Apple closer to where the market expects AI to be. I'm personally still keeping a close eye on the steady incremental improvements from the big AI labs, but I don't expect Apple to iterate Siri at breakneck speed. The new bar Siri AI has set in iOS 27 is already pretty solid.

Overall, iOS 27 is a very pleasing update in terms of performance, stability, and making the iPhone nicer to use.
